idiom_name: ScalaTest/MUnit assertions over committed golden resources (munit-snapshot for the off-the-shelf loop)
implementation_notes: ScalaTest and MUnit are runners with matchers, not baseline stores, so the harness is hand-written: write the captured output to a resource or fixture file under src/test/resources, compare with should === / assertEquals, and re-record behind an environment variable or a dedicated sbt task. munit-snapshot adds file-backed snapshot assertions to MUnit (assertNoDiff-style) when a small library is acceptable, which is the closest thing Scala has to an off-the-shelf realization; ScalaTest offers no equivalent. Scala's value semantics help as long as you pin an explicit rendering of a case class instead of the compiler-generated toString, which changes shape with the class definition.
pitfalls: Case-class toString prints every field and its shape changes whenever the class changes, so refactors break the golden; render a deliberate projection.
sbt runs tests in parallel by default, so a shared golden file must not be written concurrently - keep the update path to a single-threaded run (or a separate task).
Classpath resource loading reads from the build output; the update path must write the source tree location explicitly or new references never reach version control.
